sam: Quick heads-up — ran a 2h perf sweep on prod-staging GPUs (A100) across microbatch sizes 4/8/12. p95 steady but p99 spikes when mb >= 8 during KV churn. trace: https://grafana.redwood/prod-staging/expr/kv-flip :thinking:
lia: Can you paste the flamegraph or kernel-switch logs?
sam: Pasting a short snippet — looks like dynamic kernel fallback when ephemeral KVCACHE misses cause alloc pressure:
```
kernel_picker: selected=fused_attn
on_kv_miss -> memory_pressure -> selected=generic_attn\```
sam: That flip adds ~40-60ms to tail per affected request
mike: Oof. Is this tied to the kernel-opti change we rolled last week?
sam: Related but not identical. Last week's regression was static kernel ordering; this is a runtime flip caused by transient mem churn + larger microbatches
lia: Did you try prefetching KV or bumping the KV prewarm window?
sam: Prefetch reduces kvmiss but raises peak memory, which paradoxically triggers the fallback earlier. classic tradeoff
ana: (typo) sorry, ana: Any chance we bias the kernel-picker to prefer fused_attn with a soft threshold so tiny pressure doesn't force a flip?
jonah: We could add a "stable_kernel" hint in request metadata to pin kernel for N steps / session — avoids flip noise
mike: That will help tail but might hurt throughput if fused_attn is less memory efficient in some sequences
sam: Quick experiment: keep microbatch=8 but limit in-flight concurrency to target_util=0.75 (soft-admit). p99 improved ~25% while aggregate throughput dropped ~12%
lia: Nice — admission control seems to outperform bluntly capping MB for this workload
sam: Plan: canary a combo: soft-admit + kernel-hint header + probe metric that counts kvmiss->kernelflip events. deploy-bot: canary started on prod-staging: canary/kv-handoff-2209876543
ana: Add metric kv_kernel_flip.rate and an alert at >0.5/min. Also add a histogram tag for microbatch size
jonah: Also think about priority-aware prefetch: only prefetch for high-priority requests to avoid raising mem for everything
mike: TL;DR options: 1) cap microbatch at 6 (simple), 2) keep 8+ but enable soft-admit to limit concurrency (better p99), 3) kernel pinning + priority-prefetch for HP requests (complex but best latency/throughput mix)
lia: SGTM. I'll write a short RFC with the canary checklist + Grafana panels to watch
sam: I'll attach traces + flamegraphs to the RFC and follow up with experiment numbers :thumbsup:
